text: The rwb-case reference-data contract serves the read of a reference table by table code as GET /api/recovery/case/v1/reference-data/{tableCode} on the rwb-case base, one hop, 2 s timeout, with a fake that answers a list, an empty list and a timeout. The dictionary slice reads LOV-ROLE and the refresh-cycle list through it once per call and never writes a list as a constant. The governance load is submitted the other way round: rwb-case calls this service's reference-table handler for table code sys_fields.
why: No source names a consumer-facing read of a whole reference table, and the dictionary cannot resolve a list of values without one; DP-07 forbids a local copy and DP-11 forbids a second hop.
read: Ownership Map api GET /admin/lists/{listCode} and POST /admin/reference-loads (P3, ASM-A6-api-4); Template and Rules v1 R3 default ruling, R5.5 DP-07 and DP-11
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 1 entry check
impact: Low: one contract read in place of a monolith endpoint.

text: The five dictionary schemas take their property names from the API specification character for character; the required flags, the nullable ones and the exact string lengths are settled at the baseline review; the security scheme names the rwb_source_data login (DP-02) and no other login. The reference-table handler for table code sys_fields is part of the same baseline.
why: The contract has to be faked from Day 1 and no source fixes the required flags or the lengths; leaving them open would block the app slice.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-064 Data table; API Specification v4 dictionary and contract paths; TSD P1 v3 T-A; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-02
confirm: Tech lead at the wave 1 entry check
impact: Low: the property names already exist in the API specification.

text: Every deployment value of the dictionary slice (image digest, chart version, replicas, resources, probe paths and timings, log level, namespace, build ID, flag value, alert thresholds and windows, incident route) is a named chart value set per environment by the platform team and never hard-coded. The migration step refuses any schema but rwb_source_data, and a failed step fails the release.
why: No source carries a values file, a probe, a threshold or a route for this service, and the story cannot be tested without named values.
read: Architecture v5 slide 20 (service template); Non Functional Specification v3; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s12
confirm: DevOps lead at the wave 1 entry check

text: The sandbox is one DEV database per service release, rwb_sandbox for rwb-source-data, and the synthetic data generator is a separate build module of the rwb-source-data repository that the service artefact does not contain. It builds the 92 Workbench tables and the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views of its own schema only and reads no other service's tables.
why: Architecture v5 slide 29 forbids a cross-schema read and the legacy story describes one monolith schema; a shared sandbox would need 19 cross-schema writes.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-065 AC1 to AC9; Architecture v5 slides 11, 20 and 29; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 1 entry check
impact: Medium: one sandbox per service instead of one shared sandbox.

text: The sandbox contract is the pipeline stage interface: its input is the seed profile, its output is the built sandbox with its row counts and its checksum, and its four fixtures are a full seed, an empty seed, a refused seed and a timeout. The five profile elements are fixed in the baseline and the field-level types, lengths, required flags and pattern wording are settled at the baseline review.
why: No source describes the contract of a build stage, and the stage cannot be faked or drift-checked without a fixed input and output profile.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-065 section 12; TSD P1 v3 T3.1; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s12
confirm: Tech lead at the wave 1 entry check
impact: Low: a stage interface with no business value.

text: The sandbox is the DEV database rwb_sandbox with the build database rwb_sandbox_next, both owned by the ACE team, and the read-only role is rwb_sandbox_read with SELECT only and no DDL. No other service's schema is granted to it and the sandbox holds no data of production origin.
why: The legacy AC2 asserts readability and AC7 asserts no clear personal value, and neither names a database or a role in the 19-service target.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-065 AC2 and AC7; Ownership Map v1 (no sandbox row); Architecture v5 slides 11 and 29
confirm: ACE data architect at the wave 1 entry check
impact: Low: two database names and one role name.

text: The ledger append is POST /interactions on the rwb-source-data base. A caller without Case record C gets 403; a case that does not exist or is out of the caller's scope gets 404 with the text of MSG-P4-003; an Idempotency-Key reused with a different body gets 409; a body that fails validation gets 400 or 422; a ledger that cannot be written gets 503 with MSG-P1-022. The authorisation of the append is the session and the scope check of the rwb-case case contract, one hop, 2 s timeout.
why: The legacy writer was an in-process interface with no path and no status code, so the app slice has no interface to build against until one is fixed.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-066 AC5 to AC7; API Specification v4 Interaction resource; Ownership Map api POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions (P1, ASM-A6-api-1)
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 1 entry check
impact: Medium: fixes the one path and the error split the contract publishes.

text: The ledger resource path is /interactions on base /api/recovery/source-data/v1, the security scheme names the rwb_source_data login, and the property names are those of the API specification Interaction resource. The required flags and the exact length of each append property are settled at the baseline review, and the P3 case timeline consumes the ledger through this contract and never reads the table.
why: The API specification declares the interaction paths with x-module P3 while the Ownership Map rules the ledger to P1, and the contract cannot be published without one path.
read: API Specification v4 Interaction resource; TSD P3 v3 T-A API-P3-014 and API-P3-015; Ownership Map ruling on the ledger; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-18
confirm: Tech lead at the wave 1 entry check
impact: Medium: one path and one owner decided once.

text: Every deployment value of the ledger writer (image digest, replicas, resources, probe paths and timings, log level, namespace, build ID, flag value, alert thresholds, windows and the incident route) is a named chart value set per environment. The append failure alert uses MSG-P1-022 and the ledger incident carries the case ID, the error class and the build ID only; the trigger alert is raised when tr_interaction_append_only is missing or disabled, and the release fails in a pipeline.
why: No source gives a values file, a threshold, a window or a route, and an alert on the append-only trigger is required by the ledger design.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-066 (no deployment content); Architecture v5 slide 20; Non Functional Specification v3

text: The document fact is read as rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1 and the timer fact as rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1, rows 16 and 19 of the Architecture v5 event catalogue, and rwb-source-data is recorded as their consumer for the ledger intake only. Each producer signs off its own row of the intake map before the row is published.
why: The legacy event names EV-16 and EV-19 are not the target CloudEvents types and the catalogue lists no rwb-source-data consumer row for either fact.

The format beyond that row content is settled at the baseline review.

text: The guarantee claim read of rwb-guarantee is a C dependency with its own fake, added to the story although the Work Package does not list it, and it returns no claim until S3 is built in wave 3. The case-existence answer comes from the rwb-case case contract, faked with the same gap and assumption. Neither call is a table read and neither blocks the build.
why: The stage 2 build cannot read TCG claims without a contract, S3 is not built before wave 3, and DP-11 forbids a table read across services.

why: No source names the workflow or its activities, and the story cannot be built or tested without a fixed shape.
